clue.text: Playing by canal — time to show unashamed nature

indicators.note: playing about with something rearranges it, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone fooling about beside a canal decides it is time to drop all modesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' shuffles BY and CANAL together with T (time) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blatancy is the quality of being openly brazen, an unashamed disposition.

clue.text: Man about town plunging right in to annoy the woman

indicators.note: the letter for right plunges into the word that follows, going inside it

parts.note: to bug someone is to annoy them
her refers to the woman

explanation.surface: A city man dives straight in to irritate a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man about town' looks like a socialite, but it simply means a town's citizen; 'plunging ... in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgher is a citizen of a town, so literally a man belonging to a town.

clue.text: Rising disorder limited by more capable production-line worker

indicators.note: the second piece is bounded on both sides by the first, held within its limits

parts.note: abler means more capable

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a mess is a disorder

explanation.surface: Unrest grows on the factory floor, kept in check by a more competent operative.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Rising' reads its word upwards, and 'limited by' means held between the outer word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembler puts parts together, typically on a factory production line.

clue.text: A university chap volunteers for City

parts.note: Gus is a man's name, so a chap
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A college man signs up as a volunteer for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is a US city, capital of Maine and also a city in Georgia.

clue.text: Obtain returns seated in middle part for train

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits inside the other word

parts.note: the core is the central part

indicators.note: returns means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: Someone collects a refund while sitting in the middle carriage of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests a railway, but it is a procession of mourners following a hearse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a procession, especially at a funeral, and a train of followers is a retinue.

clue.text: Tree Lapp finally cuts in extremely high latitudes

indicators.note: the chosen letter cuts into the other word, landing inside it

parts.note: the polar regions lie at the most extreme latitudes

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word Lapp

explanation.surface: In the far north a Lapp cuts down a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes P from Lapp, which 'cuts in' puts inside POLAR: PO-P-LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing tree of the willow family.

clue.text: Belief that's unorthodox pains the monastery's head

indicators.note: something unorthodox is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An abbot is troubled by a heretical creed that annoys him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's unorthodox' rearranges PAINS THE into PANTHEIS, and 'head' takes M from monastery's.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism is a religious doctrine identifying God with the universe, a belief system.

clue.text: Stiffly formal and troubled archbishop

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means troubled

explanation.surface: A starchy, worried senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ate' here is the past tense of eat in the sense of worry or trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is the title of the chief bishop of a country or province, an archbishop.

clue.text: Wine, perhaps, put all over fish

indicators.note: the first word is spread over the second, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
the coho is a Pacific salmon

explanation.surface: A dish of fish with wine poured all over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The coho is a North Pacific salmon. 'put ... over' wraps one word round the other; 'Wine, perhaps' is an example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is one example of an alcoholic drink, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Where standards may be set to be observed?

definitions.text: Where standards may be set to be observed?

parts.words: Where standards may be set to be observed?
parts.note: standards suggests principles or flags, but here they are standard roses, grown on a tall single stem and planted out for display

explanation.surface: A question about where benchmarks get laid down for people to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a rose trained on a tall stem, planted in a garden of roses for show.

clue.text: Move slowly inside church

parts.note: in means inside

explanation.surface: Someone creeps quietly into a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move forward by small degrees, very slowly.

clue.text: Has made the path wander into capital piece of parkland

indicators.note: letters that wander move away from their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has laid a meandering footpath into a city park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wander' rearranges HAS MADE THE PATH. Hampstead Heath is a large open park in north London; 'capital' means in London.
explanation.definitionFit: This heath is a famous stretch of open ground in London, a park in the capital.

clue.text: Rare vacant tenancy agreement that's free

indicators.note: a vacant word has its inside emptied out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: a lease is a tenancy contract

explanation.surface: An unusual empty flat comes with a contract that costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' leaves only the first and last letters of Rare; 'free' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To release someone is to set them free, a verb synonym.

clue.text: The Devil's around to ruin one good person

indicators.note: the first word goes around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: Satan is the Devil; the 's stands for is
to mar is to ruin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Satan is lurking, ready to corrupt a decent soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Devil's' stands for 'is', and 'around' makes the Devil enclose the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable of the Good Samaritan, the name means a person who helps others.

clue.text: Shoot and scoot — I'm detected in a flash

parts.note: to shoot is to fire
to scoot is to dash off, fly

explanation.surface: A gunman fires and runs, only to be caught on camera by a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the insect itself, which is spotted by its glow.
explanation.definitionFit: This glowing beetle reveals itself by brief bursts of light at night.

clue.text: Less uptight about woman with new deodorant?

indicators.note: the first word is placed about the others, surrounding them

parts.note: freer means less constrained
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A more relaxed man worries about a woman's new body spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the less-uptight word surround the rest; the question mark marks deodorant as an example of a freshener.
explanation.definitionFit: A deodorant is one kind of air or body freshener, so an example.

clue.text: Never is Monteverdi showing such Italian operatic style

indicators.note: the answer is on show within the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: A claim that Monteverdi's operas never display a certain realist Italian manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across neVER IS MOnteverdi; Monteverdi is himself an Italian opera composer, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Verismo is the realistic school of late 19th-century Italian opera, as in Puccini and Mascagni.

clue.text: See about sculpture, perhaps with hard material

indicators.note: the first word is set about the others, surrounding them

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
sculpture is an example of art
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Look at a statue, maybe carved from some tough substance.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, an English cathedral city, is a crossword favourite. 'about' signals the container; 'material' means worldly.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly and material both mean worldly, of this physical world rather than spiritual.

clue.text: Rail arrived at the platform not quite eight after five

indicators.note: the eight piece comes after the five piece in the answer

parts.note: a train that has arrived at the platform is in
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A train pulls in at just before eight minutes past five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims eight to EIGH, placed 'after' V.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest loudly, which is what inveighing against something means.

clue.text: Ever so many upper-class people will be keeping private

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage

indicators.note: the people word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: men is a plural for people
PTE is the military abbreviation for private

explanation.surface: Lots of posh folk will insist on keeping things to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: U as shorthand for upper-class comes from the old U and non-U usage debate; 'will be keeping' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Articles in Europe on game experience

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is the German definite article
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: European articles about a game someone has been through.
explanation.walkthrough: The articles come from two languages: French UN and German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or go through it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Demonstrate annoying person pens rubbish

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a pest is an irritating person
rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: A nuisance writes a load of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means enclose: P-ROT-EST.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to demonstrate publicly against something.

clue.text: What's found primarily in North Atlantic region with horny appendage (long)

definitions.text: What's found primarily in North Atlantic region with horny appendage (long)

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of each word that follows

parts.words: North Atlantic region with horny appendage (long)

explanation.surface: A description of an Arctic sea creature with a long horn-like tusk.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the whale, and its words' first letters spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale whose male has a long spiralled tusk, found in northern Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Right always to finish Mass with alternative form of pious address

parts.note: ever means always
end means finish
other means alternative

explanation.surface: It is right always to conclude a Mass with a different devout greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass here is the physics symbol M, not the church service the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title used when speaking to the head of a convent, a religious style of address.

clue.text: What's driven from London to Edinburgh, abandoning English nationality

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter is left out

parts.words: What's driven from London to Edinburgh
parts.note: the A1 is the road running from London to Edinburgh, so 'the A1' is driven along it, the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A motorist heads north from London to Scotland, leaving England behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; THE A1 with 1 as I, minus E, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the nationality of people from Thailand.

clue.text: One later among these clues and this would be so unlucky?

definitions.text: One later among these clues and this would be so unlucky?

parts.words: One later among these clues and this would be so unlucky?
parts.note: this is the twelfth across clue, so one place on it is the number thought unlucky, as in Friday the 13th

explanation.surface: A superstitious remark about the next clue in the list being ill-omened.
explanation.walkthrough: Counting the across clues as printed, this entry is twelfth, so the one after it is the ordinal of the unlucky number.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is traditionally an unlucky number, and the next clue would occupy the corresponding ordinal place.

clue.text: What may be seen around prey, thickish ophidian

definitions.text: What may be seen around prey
definitions.meaning: a constrictor snake coils its body round its victim
ophidian means snake; this one is a heavy-bodied constrictor

explanation.surface: A thick snake is spotted wrapped around its catch.
explanation.definitionFit: This large constricting snake kills by coiling round prey, and is notably heavy-bodied.

clue.text: Cut short spoken exam relating to a particular thesis

indicators.note: spoken means the word is said aloud and the sound is what counts

parts.note: docked means cut short, as with a dog's tail
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A truncated viva voce examination.
explanation.walkthrough: DOCKED said aloud sounds like DOCT, giving DOCT + ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctoral thesis is the dissertation written for a doctorate degree.
